columns.rationale: Landed as VARCHAR but all 10 sample_values are integral digit strings (e.g. '10309', '1058'); null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 9057 equals row_count 9057, so it is a fully populated unique identifier cast to INTEGER.
Alphanumeric airport identifier with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 9057 equal to row_count; samples like '03N' and '07FA' are not numeric, so text is kept as-is.
Low-cardinality category with null_rate 0.0 and 5 distinct_values (heliport, large_airport, medium_airport, seaplane_base, small_airport); kept as text.
Airport display name with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 9006, samples such as 'A Coruña Airport'; kept as text.
Latitude in decimal degrees with null_rate 0.0, min -79.777778 and max 82.517263, within the valid [-90, 90] range; landed DECIMAL(38,9) retained.
Longitude in decimal degrees with null_rate 0.0, min -179.876999 and max 179.9757, within the valid [-180, 180] range; landed DECIMAL(38,9) retained.
All sample_values are integral (-1266.0 through -70.0) with min -1266.0 and max 14472.0 fitting INTEGER, so the DECIMAL(38,9) is cast down; null_rate 0.036988 (335 nulls) is retained as null.
Two-letter continent code with null_rate 0.0 and 7 distinct_values (AF, AN, AS, EU, NA, OC, SA); kept as text.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 239; samples like 'AD', 'AE' fit the two-letter pattern.
ISO 3166-2 region code with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 2169; samples like 'AD-08' and 'AF-BAL' follow the country-region pattern.
Served city or town with distinct_count 8049; null_rate 0.039748 (360 nulls) so nulls are retained rather than imputed.
Exactly 2 distinct_values ('yes', 'no') with null_rate 0.0, so the text is safely cast to BOOLEAN and renamed to make the flag semantics explicit.
Four-letter ICAO code (samples 'AGAF', 'AGAR') with distinct_count 7820; null_rate 0.136579 (1237 nulls) so nulls are retained.
Three-letter IATA code (samples 'AAA', 'AAB') with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 9057 equal to row_count, so every row carries a unique code.
GPS identifier with distinct_count 8569; null_rate 0.053881 (488 nulls) so nulls are retained.
Sparsely populated local identifier: null_rate 0.636635 (5766 nulls) with distinct_count 3193; retained nullable because the values present (e.g. '00C') carry business meaning.
Sparsely populated website URL: null_rate 0.749034 (6784 nulls) with distinct_count 2272; samples are well-formed http URLs, retained nullable.
Wikipedia URL with distinct_count 7870; null_rate 0.130838 (1185 nulls) so nulls are retained.
Sparsely populated free-text keyword list: null_rate 0.679585 (6155 nulls) with distinct_count 2883; samples mix comma-separated phrases and codes, so it is kept as raw text.
Profile marks is_airbyte_metadata true; capture-tool record UUID, not a business column.
Profile marks is_airbyte_metadata true; extraction timestamp spanning only 2026-09-02T23:26:27 to 2026-09-02T23:26:28, a capture artifact.

decisions.rationale: id has null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 9057 equal to row_count 9057, so a single id uniquely identifies each airport row; ident and iata_code are also fully unique and can serve as alternate keys, but id is the source's stable surrogate.
duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 9057, so no duplicate rows exist in bronze and the dedupe strategy is none.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are flagged is_airbyte_metadata in the profile and are dropped as pipeline columns.
All id samples are integral digit strings; the cast is strict so any future non-numeric id would fail the build rather than silently null.
elevation_ft samples are all integral with min -1266.0 and max 14472.0, so DECIMAL(38,9) is narrowed to INTEGER; 335 nulls (null_rate 0.036988) are retained.
scheduled_service has exactly two distinct values 'yes' and 'no' with no nulls, so it is cast to BOOLEAN and renamed has_scheduled_service.
local_code (null_rate 0.636635), keywords (0.679585), and home_link (0.749034) are sparsely populated but retained nullable; no imputation and no row drops.

purpose: silver_ourairports_airports is a cleaned, typed reference table of 9,057 airports from the OurAirports bronze landing, one row per airport id, feeding downstream dimensional models and geo lookups that join on id, ident, or iata_code.
usage: Join on id (the declared grain) or on the fully populated unique codes ident and iata_code. Coordinates are decimal degrees within valid ranges; elevation_ft is feet above sea level and may be null (3.7% of rows). Filter on has_scheduled_service (boolean) to restrict to airports with commercial service. Treat local_code, home_link, and keywords as optional enrichment given their high null rates.
limitations: Sparse columns are retained but mostly null: local_code is 63.7% null, keywords 68.0% null, and home_link 74.9% null; icao_code is 13.7% null and wikipedia_link 13.1% null. keywords is unstructured free text with mixed comma-separated content and is not parsed. No external validation of ISO country/region codes or URL reachability is performed in this layer.
